title: Library system: search, fines, reservations, reports (large, several modules)
command:
Implement these features in the `library` package. Keep existing public names and signatures working. Dates are datetime.date values passed in by the caller.

1. Catalog.search(query) in library/catalog.py: case-insensitive. A book matches when every whitespace-separated word of the query is a substring of its title or its author (different words may match different fields). Results are Book objects sorted by title, then id. A blank query returns all books in that order.

2. Fines in library/loans.py: return_book(book_id, on) returns the fine in cents: 25 cents for each day after the due date (returning on the due date is free), capped at 1000 cents per loan. Add the fine to the member's fines_cents and store it in the return event's "fine_cents". Add pay_fine(member_id, cents): raises ValueError if cents <= 0 or more than owed, otherwise reduces fines_cents. A member who owes 500 cents or more cannot check out (raise LoanError).

3. Reservations in library/loans.py: add reserve(book_id, member_id, on) and reservations(book_id) -> list of member ids in queue order. Only a checked-out book can be reserved; a member cannot reserve a book they currently have or have already reserved (all raise LoanError). The queue is first come, first served. When a book with reservations is returned on day D, it is held for the first member in the queue through day D+3 (inclusive): during the hold only that member may check it out (anyone else gets LoanError). If the holder has not checked it out by then, their reservation is dropped and the next member is held for the following 3 days (days D+4..D+6), and so on; once the queue is empty anyone may check it out. When the holder checks the book out, their reservation is removed. Expired holds are resolved from the date passed to checkout().

4. library/reports.py: monthly_report(events, year, month) using LoanService.events. Return {"checkouts": n, "returns": n, "fines_cents": sum of fine_cents of returns in that month, "top_books": up to 3 (book_id, checkouts) tuples for that month, most checkouts first, ties by book_id}. Events from other months are ignored.
